questions.question: A cuboid has length l, breadth b, height h. Its Lateral Surface Area (LSA) formula is:
questions.explanation: LSA of cuboid = 2h(l + b). It includes only the 4 side faces (not top and bottom). TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) includes all 6 faces. Volume = lbh.

questions.question: A cuboidal pit (l = 4 m, b = 3 m, h = 2.5 m) is dug. How many cubic metres of earth was removed?
questions.explanation: Volume of earth removed = V of pit = l×b×h = 4×3×2.5 = 30 m³.

questions.question: If all dimensions of a cuboid are doubled, by what factor does the volume increase?
questions.explanation: Original V = lbh. New V = (2l)(2b)(2h) = 8lbh. Volume increases 8 times. (Each linear dimension doubles → volume = 2³ = 8 times larger. This is why a scaled-up box holds much more.)

questions.question: A rectangular room: l = 15 m, b = 12 m, h = 5 m. Volume of air in the room =
questions.explanation: Air fills the entire cuboid. V = 15×12×5 = 900 m³. (This is used to calculate air conditioning load, ventilation requirements, etc.)

questions.question: How many small cubes (side 2 cm each) can be packed in a cuboid box (l = 16 cm, b = 12 cm, h = 8 cm)?
questions.explanation: Cubes along length: 16÷2=8. Along breadth: 12÷2=6. Along height: 8÷2=4. Total = 8×6×4 = 192. (OR: Box volume ÷ cube volume = 1,536 ÷ 8 = 192.)
